subject: Probe Loan: onboarding corridor & usage constraints
messages:
From: Jesse O'Neill <jesse.oneill@brightretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Probe Loan: onboarding corridor & usage constraints

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our ML team is keen to run a short probe against Redwood to validate latency and slice-level quality for our retail re-ranking use case. Before we open a sandbox, we need to align on a Mutual Action Plan and the usage constraints for the assets we will loan you. High level ask: a two-week canary followed by a 6-week evaluation window.

What we plan to provide:
- Prompt pack (approx. 150 curated prompts)
- Testcases (~2k examples; mix of annotations and golden outputs)
- Small metadata manifest (see attached)

Key constraints from our side:
- Assets are provided under an ephemeral, evaluation-only agreement (no production use).
- Access must be limited to an isolated sandbox (VPC peering preferred).
- Data retention: 60 days max in the sandbox, with automated takedown after expiry.
- Token budget: cap at 250k tokens during the evaluation (we can flex for canary bursts).
- Auditability: we need per-request logs (token counts, model id, timestamps) for the canary period.

Acceptance criteria:
1) 95th percentile latency target <= 120 ms for our 512-token path during the canary.
2) Re-ranking accuracy lift > 8% against our baseline on the testcases.
3) No exfiltration — prompt/testcase content must not be used outside the sandbox once the loan ends.

Can you send a short MAP with milestones (kickoff, canary, acceptance gates, takedown) and confirm that Redwood can support the VPC sandbox + token caps + automated takedown? Also send the appropriate legal contact for a short MPA amendment and the SOC2 artifacts we should expect.

Attaching: probe_sample_manifest.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Jesse
Jesse O'Neill
Head of ML Ops, BrightRetail
jesse.oneill@brightretail.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jesse O'Neill <jesse.oneill@brightretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Probe Loan: onboarding corridor & usage constraints

Jesse — thanks for the clear spec and the manifest. This is tractable and aligns with our standard probe flows. Short answers up front: yes on isolated sandbox (we support VPC peering or short-lived sandbox instances), yes on token caps, and yes on automated takedown.

Ill draft a concise MAP with milestones and an operational checklist and send it by tomorrow EOD. Proposed high-level timeline (subject to your signoff):
- Day 0: MPA sign + SOC2 evidence exchange + account provisioning
- D1-2: Sandbox provisioning + one-time key issuance (ephemeral keys)
- D3-9: Canary (2-week equivalent window can be compressed for a small burst; we recommend 10 business days)
- D10-42: Expansion evaluation window (up to 6 weeks)
- D43: Acceptance run + metrics handover
- D45: Automated takedown + archive delivery (if requested)

I'll attach our MAP draft (redwood_map_draft_v1.pdf) and a short runbook for the sandbox flow. Two asks: please confirm the retention window (you mentioned 60 days) and provide the legal contact for the MPA amendment so our contracts team can prep a one-pager.

Quick note on audit logs: we can provide per-request logs for the canary with token counts and model id. For broader logs during the evaluation window we can provide aggregated reports unless you need continuous raw logs (we can discuss retention costs).

I'll loop in Ben (sales lead) and Marissa (onboarding eng) to scope infra details.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

(quoted above)

Operational MAP (draft):
- Kickoff (Day 0): legal MPA signed; SOC2 certificate and AICPA contact provided.
- Provisioning (D1): allocate a single isolated sandbox; create ephemeral service account + keys (expires after 90 days by default; we will set to 60 if you confirm).
- Canary (D2-D11): run targeted subset (~200 testcases) to validate perf.
- Expansion (D12-D50): full testcase run, monitor quality metrics and cost telemetry.
- Acceptance gate (D51): Redwood and BrightRetail run acceptance suite; if pass, Redwood delivers an evaluation report.
- Takedown (D52-D60): automated takedown scheduled; export archived metrics and remove artifacts.

Operational constraints / configuration notes:
- Token caps: we will enforce a hard cap per service account and daily sub-quota. We can set the overall cap to 250k tokens or higher for brief bursts; any overage requires written approval.
- Audit logs: per-request logs for canary window (raw) and aggregated logs for expansion window. Raw logs retention: default 30 days; permanent export available on request.
- Data residency: sandbox will be provisioned in us-west-2 (unless you need eu region).
- Security: SOC2 Type II in the attic; we can provide a redacted report to your security team.

Attachments provided to you: sandbox-credentials-guide.md (runbook), and the MAP draft Rachel attached.

Marissa, please confirm: expected infra warm-up time, service limit changes, and whether we can automate takedown to a single click from our console.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwood.com
